title: Console walkthrough: usage analytics & cost breakdown - Sentinel Payments
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 09:23 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Rajiv Rao (Sentinel), Marta Lopez (Sentinel SecOps), Darren Ng (Sentinel ML)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and a detailed cost breakdown for their routing use case. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted, data residency and KMS integration. Agreed to run a small cost/perf benchmark and share SOC2 + network diagrams.

Topics:
- Overview of console usage analytics
- Per-route dashboards and token-level cost
- Cost levers: batching, caching, quantization, routing
- Dedicated capacity and VPC / KMS considerations
- Next steps: benchmark, pricing, security docs

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on time. I'm Lena from Redwood, AE, and with me is Marcus our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Rajiv: Doing good, thanks. We have about 40 minutes, wanted to see the console flow specifically — usage analytics and cost breakouts for our payment routing workload.
[00:10] Marcus: Great, we'll jump right in; quick note — I'll be showing the demo from our staging console, some numbers are mocked but represent typical throughput.
[00:20] Marcus: (screen share) So the first panel you'll see is the usage analytics. Top line shows total tokens, requests per minute, and a cost projection for the month. You can filter by model, route, and time window.
[00:35] Marta: Can you show per-route? We have several routes: fraud-check, reconciliation, nlp-enrichment — want to map costs.
[00:40] Marcus: Absolutely. Under routes, here's a list. For each route we expose: requests, avg latency p50/p95, token breakdown, and token-level cost. The cost column is driven by the model profile and quantization setting, and also includes batching impact.
[00:55] Darren: Interesting — is that per-token compute plus infra? How do you calculate the cost number?
[01:00] Marcus: Good question. It's a blended unit cost: model compute estimated per-token (based on our benchmarks for that model/quantization/hardware) plus estimated infra overhead. For Dedicated customers we replace the infra unit with committed capacity pricing to give you a predictable per-token.
[01:20] Rajiv: So for peak routing windows we get predictable cost with Dedicated? We need sub-100ms latencies for fraud-check.
[01:27] Lena: Yes, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can pin model variants; you can also configure autoscale/burst policies. For sub-100ms we'll show some latency dashboards and you can run a benchmark.
[01:35] Marcus: Back to the console — clicking a route opens the route dashboard. You can drill into a timeframe, see the sequence length distribution, KV cache hit rates, and request traces. And we surface the batching histogram so you can see where batching is occurring and where latency spiky requests bypass batching.
[01:55] Marta: KV cache hit rates are important for us, we cache user context for reconciliation. How granular is that metric?
[02:00] Marcus: It's per-route and per-model; we show both prefix cache hits and full KV hits per minute. There's also an export to CSV if you want to bring it into your analytics stack.
[02:15] Darren: Any guidance in console on how batching impacts latency vs cost?
[02:20] Marcus: Yes — on the right-hand side we have cost levers and recommendations (Optimize). For example, if you increase batch window to 25ms you might save ~12% on tokens for high-concurrency routes; the console simulates the latency trade-off using your p95 SLA. It also suggests enabling prefix caching for repeat patterns.
[02:40] Rajiv: Does Optimize do quantization suggestions automatically? We use large open models and want to reduce GPU costs.
[02:45] Marcus: It does. Optimize will recommend quantization profiles by workload; we have pre-validated profiles for MQA and int8 variants. It flags any estimated quality delta so product teams can review.
[02:58] Marta: From a security perspective — where is the data stored and how are logs handled?
[03:03] Lena: For Hosted API, we have short-term ephemeral stores and configurable retention; for Private/Dedicated the logs and data plane can be kept in customer VPC and we support KMS/HSM integrations. We also provide audit logs in the console and can export to your SIEM.
[03:20] Marta: Are you SOC 2 and ISO certified?
[03:23] Lena: We're SOC 2 certified and have ISO assessment in progress; we'll share the security pack after this call.
[03:30] Marcus: Jumping back to the route cost graph — you can break down cost by model, token type (input vs output), and by feature flags (like streaming vs non-streaming). Filtering to fraud-check, you can see that output tokens are driving 70% of cost due to long explanation generation.
[03:50] Rajiv: We generate fairly long outputs for investigations; can we cap output tokens per route?
[03:55] Marcus: Yes — routing policies let you set max_output_tokens per route and also a fallback to a smaller model or a condensed summarizer when token counts exceed threshold. That shows up in the console as potential cost savings.
[04:10] Darren: We also want to estimate what moving to Dedicated would save us monthly. Can the console model that?
[04:15] Marcus: There's a 'what-if' cost modeller: enter your current RPM and output length distribution and it will compare Hosted vs Dedicated with projected savings factoring in reserved commit levels. We can run that for your actual trace data if you share a sample.
[04:30] Rajiv: We'll want that — and also a latency benchmark for the fraud-check route, ideally from our region.
[04:36] Marcus: We can schedule a benchmark. For benchmarks we can run our agent in your VPC or run a synthetic load from our region, depending on what you prefer.
[04:45] Marta: Regarding KMS and key rotation — do you allow customer-managed keys and bring-your-own-key?
[04:50] Lena: Yes, BYOK is supported in Private and Dedicated with KMS. For Hosted we offer integration with major cloud KMS providers.
[04:58] Darren: A couple more technical clarifications — how does fallback routing work if a model is unavailable?
[05:03] Marcus: We have routing policies that can fail over to a smaller variant or to a cached response, and you can set SLO thresholds to trigger failover. The console surfaces failover counts and success rates.
[05:15] Rajiv: Any existing customers in payments? Curious about PCI and logs.
[05:19] Lena: We have a few customers in finserv; for PCI scope we recommend Private with on-prem options — our security team will walk you through the controls.
[05:28] Marta: Ok, looks good. On the console, can I set alerting on cost spikes?
[05:32] Marcus: Yes — you can create alerts for token spend, route RPM, latencies. Alerts can route to PagerDuty, Slack, or email.
[05:40] Rajiv: Great. Can you show the trace view for a single request?
[05:43] Marcus: Sure — here's a sample request trace. You can see step-by-step: ingress, routing decision, model call, KV cache hit, and the total token counts. There's also a raw transcript export.
[06:00] Darren: A lot of our concerns are around accuracy regressions when quantizing. How do you guard against silent regressions?
[06:06] Marcus: We integrate evals into the rollout workflow. Before a quantized variant is rolled out you can run your prompt set and flag accept/reject criteria. Console will show quality deltas and regression alerts post-deploy.
[06:22] Rajiv: Timeline — we're looking at a pilot in 6 weeks, full production in Q3.
[06:27] Lena: That timeline sounds reasonable. Next steps we'll outline at the end.
[06:30] (demo continues, showing CSV export and alert configuration)
[07:10] Marcus: Quick note on telemetry: we keep token-level telemetry but can anonymize it and scrub PII based on route rules before storing for analytics.
[07:25] Marta: Important for us. Also want proof of encryption at rest for all logs.
[07:29] Lena: We'll share the encryption diagrams in the security pack.
[07:35] Rajiv: On billing — do you provide line-item invoices by route? We need that for chargebacks to teams.
[07:41] Marcus: Yes, for Enterprise/Dedicated customers we can provide per-route billing and attach tags so you can do internal chargebacks.
[07:50] (questions about contractual SLAs and uptime)
[08:05] Lena: We have SLA options on Dedicated and Premium support tiers, we'll include the SLA language in the quote.
[08:13] Rajiv: Ok, recap and next steps please.
[08:17] Lena: Recap — Marcus will put together: 1) Dedicated vs Hosted what-if cost model based on a sample trace, 2) schedule a latency benchmark for fraud-check route (preferred region), 3) share SOC2 pack, KMS and network diagrams, and 4) pricing/commit options for Dedicated.
[08:34] Marcus: I'll also include instructions for running the benchmarking agent in your VPC and a short demo recording.
[08:41] Marta: Thanks, if you can send the security docs to Marta and Rajiv that's great.
[08:45] Rajiv: We'll aim to provide a sample trace by Friday.
[08:48] Lena: Great — we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark and send materials. Thanks everyone.
[08:52] (meeting ends)

End of transcript.
next_steps: Marcus to run what-if cost model and share comparison (Hosted vs Dedicated)
Schedule latency benchmark for fraud-check route (Marcus + Sentinel) - target next week
Lena to send SOC2 pack, KMS and network diagrams to Marta and Rajiv
Send pricing/commit options and SLA language
